liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Morning Dew** (1 review): Reviewer says Morning Dew and The Other One leading into Wharf Rat are worth the download alone [12]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): Not Fade Away into Goin' Down the Road Feeling Bad and back, then Johnny B. Goode, follows Good Lovin' [10]
- **Johnny B. Goode** (1 review): Reviewer hears it played at an extremely fast, hard-driving pace, faster than any other version they know [10]

## The recordings

- **gd71-02-23.sbd.orf.113.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 24 songs; 173 min; rated 4.64/5 by 11 [1]. Said about its sound: The mix takes a while to settle; Bill and Phil sit high in it, with Jerry's guitar not far forward [9]
- **gd1971-02-23.sbd.miller.110353.flac16**: soundboard; 24 songs; 172 min; rated 4.33/5 by 12 [2]
- **gd1971-02-23.sbd.evans-waddell.GEMS.82755.flac16**: soundboard; 24 songs; 164 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [3]
- **gd1971-02-23.151503.aud.partial.lamarre.vernon.sirmick.flac24**: audience recording; 12 songs; 86 min [4]. Said about its sound: Uploader rebalanced some tracks to bring up Jerry's guitar [4]

## Around the show

- The theater was a funky place with bench seats, and often freezing in winter [8]
- Port Chester had an 18-year-old drinking age during this week of shows [9]
- Jerry plays a sunburst Les Paul, Bobby a 335, Phil an SG, and Ron a Hammond B-3 [18]
- Blue Ron, not T.C., is on keyboards here, though reviewer thinks T.C. was the better player [18]
- Like much of early 1971, the band played tight and dirty, one of several great shows in this run [8]
- The sound for this winter run is much clearer than the 1970 shows at the Capitol [9]
- This show has a different feeling from the other five shows of the run [12]
- Reviewer claims Wharf Rat, Greatest Story, Johnny B. Goode, Loser, Playing in the Band and Bertha were all first played here [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1971-02-23.sbd.miller.110353.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> CD [2]. Also: Uploader says this source is a huge upgrade over all circulating copies, with seamless disc changes [2]
- **gd1971-02-23.sbd.evans-waddell.GEMS.82755.flac16**: taped by DAT from the collection of Todd Evans; transferred by Editing and Mastering in Wavelab6.0 and Ozone. Dithered L2type1ultra by Jamie Waddell; source: SBD -> Master Reel (7 inch reels @ 7.5ips 1/2trk) -> PCM -> Dat (44.1k) [3]. Also: Upgrade of earlier source: an 8000 Hz ringing tone was carefully removed without any noise reduction software; Reel flips occur in Bobby McGee and at the end of Wharf Rat; Digital zippers were patched in Me and My Uncle, and Good Lovin' was patched using shnid 113 [3]
- **gd1971-02-23.151503.aud.partial.lamarre.vernon.sirmick.flac24**: taped by Unknown; transferred by SIRMick & Matt Vernon; source: Unknown aud (3rd gen cassette) - From the collection of Doug Lamarre [4]. Also: This partial audience recording had pitch adjustments, and gain surges were smoothed out [4]
